extracted.intended_audience: SEC registrants (public companies), counsel/compliance officers, preparers of SEC filings, investors, auditors and assurance providers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for public company climate-related disclosures (alignment with TCFD/ISSB/CSRD, GHG emissions reporting, targets, assurance, timeliness, and placement in SEC filings). Intended to help registrants prepare disclosures that meet SEC final rules and consider international frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with TCFD or comparable disclosure regime
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the TCFD framework or a comparable disclosure regime to describe climate-related risks and the measures adopted to reduce and adapt to such risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release repeatedly references alignment with TCFD as a baseline; many jurisdictions' requirements and third-party frameworks (ISSB, CSRD/ESRS, GRI, SASB, CDP) are aligned to varying degrees with the TCFD recommendations. Registrants listed or operating in other jurisdictions may already be subject to TCFD-aligned requirements. Differences across frameworks in scope/definitions and intended audience can affect comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory timing for GHG disclosures (Scope 1/2/3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies subject to the Climate Corporate Data Accountability Act must disclose Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions beginning in 2026 and Scope 3 emissions beginning in 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule anticipates many registrants will already have systems in place because of overlapping federal/state/international requirements. The phased timeline means Scope 1/2 disclosures come earlier than Scope 3; registrants should prepare systems accordingly and note differences in expected coverage rates by filer size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report climate‑related financial risks and measures (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies subject to the Climate-Related Financial Risk Act must begin reporting their climate-related financial risks and measures in 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reporting obligation is separate from GHG emission metrics and includes narrative and quantitative information about how climate-related risks affect operations and financial condition. Overlap with other disclosure regimes should be identified to avoid duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCFD: Governance — board and management roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the board's oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities and describe management's role in assessing and managing climate-related risks and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party analysis finds relatively low rates of disclosure on these items (e.g., 17% for board oversight, 10% for management role in one sample), indicating many registrants do not yet provide robust governance disclosures. Firms should explicitly state governance structures, responsibilities, and escalation processes to improve investor comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCFD: Strategy — identified risks, impacts, and resilience under scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the climate-related risks and opportunities identified over the short, medium, and long term; describe the impact of such risks and opportunities on the organization's business, strategy, and financial planning; and describe the resilience of the organization's strategy, taking into consideration different climate-related scenarios, including a 2°C or lower scenario.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of scenario analysis and strategic resilience is uncommon (e.g., 5% disclosure rate for resilience under scenarios in one analysis). Registrants should provide specific, decision‑relevant discussion of scenarios, assumptions, and quantified impacts where possible to meet investor needs for forward-looking information.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCFD: Risk Management — processes and integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the organization's processes for identifying, assessing, and managing climate-related risks and explain how those processes are integrated into the organization's overall risk management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed disclosure rates for process descriptions are low (e.g., 15–17% in cited samples). Firms should document procedures, governance lines, tools used (e.g., risk registers, metrics), frequency of review, and how climate risk feeds into enterprise risk management to improve comparability and investor understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: TCFD: Metrics and Targets — metrics, GHG disclosures, and targets/performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the metrics used to assess climate-related risks and opportunities in line with strategy and risk management; disclose Scope 1, Scope 2, and, if appropriate, Scope 3 GHG emissions and the related risks; and describe the targets used to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and performance against targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure rates for metrics/targets are variable (e.g., 21% for metrics, 19% for GHGs, 25% for targets in one analysis). Registrants should disclose definitions, boundaries, methodologies, units, time periods, base years, and progress against targets. Expect different disclosure onset dates by scope per the rule (Scope 1/2 earlier than Scope 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure placement and filing context
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related information may be presented in various parts of SEC filings (Risk Factors, MD&A, Description of Business, Legal Proceedings); registrants should consider where within filings to place climate disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey data show most registrants that disclose place climate information in Risk Factors (82%), MD&A (26%), and Description of Business (19%). The release notes heterogeneity in coverage, location, and presentation across companies, which complicates investor navigation and comparability; consistent placement across filings facilitates investor analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague or boilerplate disclosures; disclose material information
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures should be specific, non‑boilerplate, and should not strategically omit material adverse information about climate-related risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters and academic studies report widespread use of vague/boilerplate language and potential underreporting of material climate-related information under a purely principles-based regime. Registrants should avoid generic statements and provide tailored, material disclosures with quantitative context where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide climate-related data and decision‑relevant disclosures in a timely manner relative to fiscal periods; reliance on sustainability reports published long after fiscal year-end reduces decision relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry observers report many sustainability reports are released more than 12 months after fiscal year end; registrants should aim for timeliness suitable for investors (e.g., within annual reporting timelines) to ensure usefulness for investment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limitations of third‑party reporting frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: When following third-party frameworks (SASB, GRI, TCFD, CDP, ISSB, CSRD/ESRS), disclose which frameworks are followed and recognize that voluntary use often results in partial or inconsistent disclosure across framework components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys indicate varied adoption rates (e.g., SASB, GRI, TCFD, CDP); alignment with TCFD differs by framework and element. Registrants should explain scope/definitions used, any deviations, and crosswalks to facilitate comparability given fragmentation across frameworks and reporting channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose climate-related targets, transition plans, and net-zero commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: If the company has targets or goals (e.g., emission reduction initiatives, science-based targets, net-zero plans) or a transition plan, disclose the existence, scope, ambition, and performance against those targets and whether plans are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data show varying prevalence by company size and index membership (e.g., higher rates among LAF/S&P 500 companies). Registrants should state whether targets are science-based, the target dates, base years, coverage (Scopes), and whether transition plans align with temperature goals (e.g., 1.5°C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party assurance of climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: When using third-party assurance, disclose the scope and level of assurance, and the assurance standard used (e.g., ISO 14064-3, AICPA, AA1000, IAASB ISAE, or other standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance use is concentrated among larger firms; for many companies assurance is limited to GHG emissions (58%) rather than entire reports (3%). The vast majority of assurance reported is limited assurance (~92%) and only a small share is reasonable assurance (~5%). Registrants should disclose the assurance provider type and the standard applied to help investors assess reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparability and consistency to aid investor analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure disclosures are consistent and comparable across periods and with peers to enable investor benchmarking and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release emphasizes that heterogeneity in topics, locations, and definitions across registrants hampers investor ability to compare disclosures. Companies should adopt clear definitions, consistent metrics, and mapping to recognized frameworks to reduce fragmentation and facilitate investor data collection and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of data sources and coverage disclosure (databases and reporting completeness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose whether third‑party databases (e.g., Refinitiv, Bloomberg, CDP) were used and the scope/coverage of reported GHG emissions and other climate data; acknowledge limitations of dataset completeness and lags.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission staff notes data collection lags (GHG disclosure can lag by up to 18 months) and estimates of coverage differences across filer status; registrants should disclose methodology, data sources, and any limitations or estimated completeness to help interpret reported metrics.
